blocks.text: How Foreclosures & Court-Ordered Sales Work in Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: In British Columbia, foreclosures and court-ordered sales are governed by the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Law and Equity Act. When a lender obtains an Order Nisi and a subsequent Conduct of Sale order, the property is listed on the MLS® at fair market value. Unlike standard residential resales, a court-ordered sale requires the lender's Schedule 'A' Addendum, which strips out standard seller warranties and states the property is sold 'as is, where is' upon possession.

Once the first acceptable offer is negotiated with the conduct-of-sale lawyer and conditions are removed by the first buyer, a court hearing date is scheduled at the New Westminster or Vancouver registry. Any competing buyers may submit sealed, unconditional (subject-free) competing bids at the courthouse hearing, so completing your building inspection, strata review, financing approval, and City of Maple Ridge permit check before court is essential.

blocks.text: Due Diligence Before Bidding on a Maple Ridge Court-Ordered Sale

parts.t: Before submitting a first offer or a competing sealed bid in court on a Maple Ridge foreclosure, we pull the BC Land Title Office title search to verify the foreclosing mortgagee and all financial encumbrances, check Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 and building permit records, and—for strata properties in East Central, West Central, or Albion—review two years of strata minutes, the Form B Information Certificate, and the depreciation report.

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales

parts.t: How does a court-ordered foreclosure sale work in Maple Ridge?

A lender with a BC Supreme Court Conduct of Sale order lists the property on the MLS®. An initial buyer negotiates an offer with subjects, removes those subjects after inspection and financing, and triggers a court approval hearing where competing buyers may submit sealed, unconditional bids.
What is the Schedule A Addendum in a BC foreclosure?

Schedule 'A' is the court-mandated addendum attached to the Contract of Purchase and Sale. It overrides standard contract clauses so the seller (the foreclosing lender) makes no representations or warranties regarding the property's condition, appliances, permits, or occupancy.
Can I include financing and inspection conditions on a Maple Ridge foreclosure?

Yes, if you are the first buyer whose offer brings the property to court, you can include standard financing, home inspection, title, and strata document conditions. However, if a court date is already set and you are submitting a competing bid at the hearing, your offer must be completely unconditional (subject-free) with a bank draft deposit.
Are Maple Ridge foreclosures sold below market value?

Under BC Supreme Court rules, the conduct-of-sale party has a legal duty to expose the property to the open MLS® market and obtain fair market value. Discounts typically reflect deferred maintenance, 'as-is' risk, or occupancy delays rather than automatic below-market pricing.
What happens to existing tenants or former owners in a foreclosure?

The Order Approving Sale granted by the judge typically includes a Writ of Possession date requiring the occupants to vacate, though buyers should confirm whether a residential tenancy under the BC Residential Tenancy Act survives the court order.
How do I check for unpermitted work on a Maple Ridge foreclosure?

Because the lender provides no Property Disclosure Statement (PDS), we verify property records, zoning under Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, and any open municipal bylaw or building files before you remove conditions or bid in court.
